transcript.content: Hi, I’m Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
My doctor says I’ve gotten too thin. My work pants are hanging loose on me, so I can see it, but… part of me still feels relieved when the number on the scale goes down.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes. If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I worry the rest of the day that it’s going to show on me. I keep checking myself and thinking I need to make up for it somehow.
When you look at your body, do you feel fat even though other people say you are too thin?
Yes… I know people say I’m too thin, but if my stomach looks even a little full in the mirror, I feel like I’ve let myself go. When I stay small and neat, it feels like I’m handling things right.
Have you been deliberately eating less to keep your weight down?
Yes. I make meals for my husband and mother-in-law, but when it’s my turn to eat, I usually just have coffee, a few vegetables, or maybe half a piece of toast. I tell myself that’s enough.
Has your weight dropped to a level your doctor says is underweight for your height?
Yes. My doctor says I’ve gotten too thin. My work pants are hanging loose on me now, though… part of me still feels relieved when I see the number on the scale go down.
